real_qa.q: How does Hotels by Day solve the technical limitation that prevents major hotel booking platforms from offering same-day room bookings?
real_qa.r: Hotels by Day connects to a channel management system that bypasses the central reservation system (CRS), which is 40-year-old technology designed only for night stays and cannot process day bookings. Instead of routing through the CRS, they connect directly to the channel manager going straight into the hotel, allowing them to access and sell inventory sitting empty between 9 AM and 6 PM.
real_qa.requete: Hotels by Day technology CRS workaround

real_qa.q: Why did Hotels by Day decide not to pursue a full patent after filing a provisional patent?
real_qa.r: Giannis realized after filing a provisional patent that the technology was not the perfect solution and would need continuous rebuilding based on individual hotel requirements. Since the sales cycle with major hotel chains like Marriott, Hilton, or Wyndham takes three to five years, and each hotel has different technology needs, committing to a patent would have locked them into a suboptimal approach with limited resources.
real_qa.requete: Hotels by Day provisional patent decision

real_qa.q: What was Hotels by Day's revenue and booking performance in the year they appeared on Shark Tank?
real_qa.r: By the time of their Shark Tank appearance, Hotels by Day had generated approximately $127,000 in gross booking revenue from 6,500 bookings in 2015, with the company taking a 14% commission. By May of the following year, they had scaled to $300,000 in revenue with 20% month-to-month growth.

real_qa.q: Why did Giannis Malti intentionally set a high ask on Shark Tank despite appearing on the show?
real_qa.r: Giannis deliberately structured their Shark Tank pitch with a high valuation ask because they primarily wanted brand awareness and booking growth rather than a Shark Tank investor. They believed a Shark Tank investor would actually harm their credibility with later-stage investors and preferred to remain independent to pursue institutional capital from investors with hospitality expertise.
real_qa.requete: Shark Tank Hotels by Day deal strategy

real_qa.q: What conversion rate does Hotels by Day see in New York city for same-day room bookings?
real_qa.r: Hotels by Day sees an 8% conversion rate among visitors who log into their site from New York and convert into a day stay booking. If they could replicate that 8% conversion across the top visitor cities, they projected reaching 12,000 bookings and generating approximately $28,000 monthly in gross revenue.
real_qa.requete: Hotels by Day New York conversion rate

real_qa.q: What hotel chains and properties had signed partnerships with Hotels by Day by the time of their Shark Tank appearance?
real_qa.r: Hotels by Day had signed every major hotel brand individually, with 300 properties across their network by the time they pitched on Shark Tank. Despite these partnerships, individual hotel technology constraints limited their ability to scale uniformly across all properties.
real_qa.requete: Hotels by Day hotel brand partnerships

guest.bio_context: Giannis Malti is the CEO and co-founder of Hotels by Day, a travel platform that enables same-day hotel room bookings for travelers with layovers or brief city visits. He appeared on Shark Tank in his second year of business after initially refusing an invitation in his first year, believing the platform needed more maturity before seeking investor attention.
